explanation: Choice A is correct. The sine of an angle is equal to the sine of $n(2\pi)$ radians more than the angle, where $n$ is an integer constant. Since $\frac{305\pi}{4}$ is equivalent to $38(2\pi) + \frac{\pi}{4}$ (because $38 \times 8 = 304$, so $\frac{305\pi}{4} - \frac{304\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{4}$), $\sin\left(\frac{305\pi}{4}\right)$ can be rewritten as $\sin\left(38(2\pi) + \frac{\pi}{4}\right)$, which is equal to $\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$. Therefore, the value of $\sin\left(\frac{305\pi}{4}\right)$ is $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$. Alternate approach: The sine of a number $t$ is the y-coordinate of the point resulting from traveling a distance of $t$ counterclockwise from the point $(1, 0)$ around a unit circle centered at the origin. A unit circle has circumference $2\pi$, so traveling $\frac{305\pi}{4}$ counterclockwise means traveling around the circle $38$ full times plus an additional $\frac{\pi}{4}$, landing at the point $\left(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)$. The y-coordinate of this point is $\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$.
